transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

The foreclosure notices started coming, and I just feel like I’m coming apart. I’ve been crying in my truck before work, and every time the phone rings I jump. I’m snapping at the apprentices, and I’ve been making stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I normally wouldn’t make.
Before these foreclosure notices started coming, were you already feeling this anxious and overwhelmed?
No. I was doing fine before all this started. Once the letters and calls began, though—within a few weeks—it felt like things at home and at work just started falling apart.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in doing things you normally enjoy?
Yeah. I’ve stopped doing a lot of things I used to keep up with—church volunteering, my fitness classes, truck-club outings. At work they’ve even taken me out of the high-risk repair bay.
Have you been feeling down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’d say most of the day, every day. I’ve been overwhelmed and upset, but it kind of comes and goes.
Do you find that thoughts about the foreclosure are constantly on your mind and difficult to push away?

Yes. It’s like I can’t get it out of my head. Since those notices started, I feel like I’m coming apart—I’ll cry in my truck before work, and every time the phone rings I jump. It’s affecting everything.
